answer: Filling 27 aliases as a result needs 27 distinct prompts, so the operator forfeits the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. Because the ripple index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the umber audit republishes the digest set at close. Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a basalt index of commitments rather than against the text alone. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
